final_rationale: The verdict does not change because no genuinely new admissible evidence was provided; the Actor reframed the same record and made concessions that largely confirm the initial audit concerns. That reframing is useful and more policy-bounded, but it does not satisfy the missing compliance predicate. Under the cited policy, rollout controls and monitoring mitigate a material model-card weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or reviewed risk acceptance exists. The admissible summary shows neither. This means the unresolved limitation is not merely a caveat attached to an otherwise compliant case; it is the missing condition needed to support the mitigation theory. For that reason, the narrowed position does not rise to compliant_with_caveats on the present record.
remaining_concerns: The affected Spanish-language billing use case remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
No approved risk acceptance is shown for that exposed limitation.
The policy text makes exclusion of the affected use case or reviewed risk acceptance a predicate for relying on rollout controls and monitoring as mitigation.
No admissible policy text shows that disclosure alone authorizes certification when the material limitation remains exposed.
The actor's narrowed position is more accurate, but its requested compliance outcome still exceeds what the summarized evidence proves.
